answer: A concrete defense is a triple-domain bond: each identity must prove live work in three isolated compute regions that do not share caches, clocks, or peer sets. One region is a high-latency tundra path that only accepts delayed attestations; another is a sealed island with no outbound reuse of proofs; the third is an interactive oasis that issues unpredictable challenges. Because proofs cannot be copied across regions, spinning up N fake agents costs N times the hardware, bandwidth, and locked stake. Multiplexing one machine fails when those challenge windows overlap.
